name: Camel
information_for_contributors: Kept in step with include/camel/parse/syntax/token_kinds.def (keywords, operators) and the grammar of the language reference (contexts).
scripts/check-grammar.mjs checks the keyword, operator and built-in type tables against
those files: the 'keywords', 'builtin-types', 'operators' and 'punctuation' rules below must
stay lists of plain 'match' patterns, keywords as \b(?:a|b|c)\b alternations.
The contextual keywords of the 'contextual-keywords' rule are the words of the one table of
scripts/context-keywords.mjs, which the language reference prints (02, 2.4.1); a word is added
or taken away in that table first, and editors/vscode/scripts/check-grammar.mjs checks this

command.comment: COMMAND: '#!' on the first line only (an interpreter line); '#' elsewhere opens a tag.
command.name: meta.preprocessor.command.camel

patterns.comment: MULTI_STR, single quotes. The lexer ends it at the first ''' whatever precedes.
patterns.name: string.quoted.triple.single.camel

patterns.comment: MULTI_STR, double quotes.
patterns.name: string.quoted.triple.double.camel

patterns.comment: STRING, double quotes. May span lines: the lexer's '.' matches a newline.
patterns.name: string.quoted.double.camel

patterns.comment: STRING, single quotes.
patterns.name: string.quoted.single.camel

patterns.comment: FSTRING, backticks. `${EXPR}` and `${EXPR:SPEC}` interpolate; `${` is opened only there, `\${` is a literal '${' and any other brace is literal.
patterns.name: string.interpolated.backtick.camel

string-escape.comment: What decodeEscapes (include/camel/utils/escape.h) decodes: the named escapes, `\0`, `\xHH` and `\u{H...}`. Any other backslash pair is kept as written (an unknown escape, e.g. the cancelled octal `\101`), but still hides a quote from the lexer.

string-escape-in-triple.comment: The same escapes, except that a backslash does not hide the closing quotes of a multi-line string.

fstring-escape.comment: `\${` is the literal '${'; everywhere else a backslash escapes as in a string (`\\`, `\``).

fstring-interpolation.comment: An interpolation: an arbitrary Camel expression, and after a ':' the format specification (as `format` takes one). TextMate cannot balance braces, so a `}` inside a nested block or struct literal of the expression ends it early; the compiler has no such limit.
fstring-interpolation.name: meta.interpolation.camel

patterns.name: constant.other.placeholder.camel
patterns.comment: A format specification starts with a colon, directly after the expression: it must begin with a specifier character, so the colon of a struct field written as `: x` is not one (TextMate cannot know the nesting).

string-placeholder.comment: A placeholder of the library function 'format': {} or {:spec}.
string-placeholder.name: constant.other.placeholder.camel

decorator.comment: funcAnno: '@' identRef angledValues? ahead of a function declaration or a block. '@' is also a binary operator, so a decorator is recognised at the start of a line only.
decorator.name: meta.decorator.camel

contextual-keywords.comment: The contextual keywords of scripts/context-keywords.mjs and of the table of the language reference (02, 2.4.1): a word that is a keyword in one position and an ordinary name everywhere else. Each pattern names its words after 'contextual keywords:' and scopes them only where the parser reads them (checked by scripts/check-grammar.mjs, pinned by test/cases/tools/grammar/context_keywords.cml).

patterns.comment: contextual keywords: 'tag', 'rule', 'fact', 'resource' — the head of a tag, rule, fact or resource declaration: the name after the word, then the token that makes it a declaration (tagDecl / ruleDecl / factDecl / resourceDecl, grammar 8.5).
contextual keywords: 'unordered' — a resource declaration whose effects keep no written order: `resource net unordered` ends there.
patterns.name: storage.type.contextual-declaration.camel

patterns.comment: contextual keywords: 'on' — the tag declaration's list of positions, which starts at the position name after it.
patterns.name: keyword.other.contextual-clause.camel

patterns.comment: contextual keywords: 'read_by' — the passes that read a tag, after its positions.
patterns.name: keyword.other.contextual-clause.camel

patterns.comment: contextual keywords: 'when' — a function's or a rule's condition (after the parameters and the return type) and a tag declaration's, before the body. The word is scoped only there, so `let when = 4` stays a name.
contextual keywords: 'uses' — a resource clause names the resources a function touches, written after `uses`.
patterns.name: keyword.other.contextual-clause.camel

patterns.comment: contextual keywords: 'pure' — a resource clause promising no resource at all.
patterns.name: keyword.other.contextual-clause.camel

patterns.comment: contextual keywords: 'join', 'meet', 'widen', 'narrow' — the trailing clauses of a fact declaration: on the line that closes its body, or on a line of their own, as the formatter writes them. Each names the function that follows it.
contextual keywords: 'join', 'meet', 'widen', 'narrow' — the same clauses on a line of their own.

contextual keywords: 'operator' — directly after `func`, when the operator it defines follows. The match starts at `func`, so that it is tried before the function-declaration rule, which reads the same two words as a name; the declarations this pattern takes get the scopes that rule gives them.
contextual keywords: 'struct', 'tuple' — in a `match type` case pattern they name a shape, not a type (typeCasePattern, grammar 8.5).
patterns.name: keyword.other.contextual-position.camel

patterns.comment: contextual keywords: 'error' — the pattern of a failed `T!` in a `case` is two words, `error e`.
patterns.name: keyword.other.contextual-position.camel

patterns.comment: contextual keywords: 'leaf' — the shape of a value with no parts, written `#leaf` as the pattern of a `match type` case.
patterns.name: keyword.other.contextual-position.camel

patterns.comment: contextual keywords: 'fields' — the head of a `static for` or `static loop` walks the fields of the type written after it.
patterns.name: keyword.other.contextual-position.camel

patterns.comment: contextual keywords: 'indices' — the same head walks the positions of the value written after it.
patterns.name: keyword.other.contextual-position.camel

patterns.comment: contextual keywords: 'field', 'nodes', 'param' — the positions of a tag, named after `on` or after a comma of that list (`func` and `type` are reserved keywords listed by the 'keywords' rule).
patterns.name: keyword.other.tag-position.camel

import-declaration.comment: importDecl: IMPORT (moduleName | (identDef | bracedIdents) FROM moduleName); moduleName: ('.' | '..' | '...')? IDENTIFIER ('.' IDENTIFIER)*

namespace-declaration.comment: namespaceDecl: NAMESPACE identRef '{' ...; usingNamespaceDecl: USING NAMESPACE identRef

with-parameters.comment: funcDecl: (WITH angledParams)? ... FUNC; ruleDecl: (WITH angledParams)? 'export'? RULE ...
with-parameters.name: meta.with-parameters.camel

function-declaration.comment: funcDecl: ... FUNC identRef parentParams (':' typeExpr)? stmtBlock
function-declaration.name: meta.function.definition.camel

type-declaration.comment: typeDecl: implMark? TYPE identRef ('=' | '<' identDef (',' identDef)* ','? ('>' '=' | '>=')) (typeExpr | STRING)

let-declaration.comment: dataDecl: LET carrier (':' typeList)? '=' dataList. The names of the carrier are immutable bindings.
let-declaration.name: meta.declaration.let.camel

var-declaration.comment: dataDecl: VAR carrier (':' typeList)? '=' dataList. The names of the carrier are mutable variables.
var-declaration.name: meta.declaration.var.camel

parameter-name.comment: keyParamPair: VAR? identDef ':' typeExpr ('=' dataExpr)?, and the name of a named argument (keyValuePair: identDef ':' dataExpr).

keywords.comment: Every keyword of include/camel/parse/syntax/token_kinds.def, each exactly once (checked by scripts/check-grammar.mjs).

wildcard.comment: pattern: '_' is a token of its own, not an identifier.
wildcard.name: variable.language.wildcard.camel

builtin-types.comment: The names src/compile/gct/builder.cpp puts in the root type scope (checked by scripts/check-grammar.mjs).

numbers.comment: REAL: [0-9]+ '.' [0-9]+ EXPONENT?; INTEGER: (DEC | OCT 0o[0-7]+ | HEX | BIN). A decimal that starts with 0 and has another digit (09, 077) is a lexical error, not two tokens. No digit separators and no suffixes. A sign directly before the digits belongs to the token.

pipe-target.comment: linkExpr: compExpr (('->' | '?->') compExpr)*. A name on the right is the function the left side is passed to.

calls.comment: annoExpr: a '(' or '<' directly after an expression (isAdjacent) is a call or a with-argument list.

member-access.comment: accessExpr / memberAccess: '.' (IDENTIFIER | INTEGER). In 't.0.1' the lexer takes '0.1' for a REAL, so the index rule leaves that form to the number rules.

angle-arguments.comment: angledValues / specType arguments: '<' directly after a name, or after the '::' that declares type parameters at the head (`func f::<T>`; design principles 5.5). The parser tells it from a comparison by adjacency (isAdjacent), and so does this rule. '>=' is one token and never closes the list.
angle-arguments.name: meta.angle-arguments.camel

operators.comment: The operators and separators of include/camel/parse/syntax/token_kinds.def, longest first (checked by scripts/check-grammar.mjs).

patterns.comment: T! (may have failed) and the postfix x!: directly after a type or an expression.
patterns.name: keyword.operator.type.camel

patterns.comment: Type operators: T? and A & B, A \ B. '|' is not one: there are no union types, and the single pipe is the ordinary or operator (the pattern above).
patterns.name: keyword.operator.type.camel
